result.stdout:
Usage: unprotect [options] [FILE]

Cross-platform decrypt-at-rest CLI for files produced by protect. Auto-selects backend (DPAPI / Keychain / libsecret) from the WPRT header marker.

Options:
  --in-place                   Replace FILE atomically via temp + rename. Mutually exclusive with --output.
  --rm                         Delete source FILE after successful round-trip verification.
  --remove-source              Alias for --rm.
  -k, --keep                   Retain source FILE (explicit default; accepted for symmetry with --rm).
  --no-verify                  Skip the post-encrypt round-trip integrity check (encrypt path only). Faster, less safe.
  -f, --force                  Overwrite an existing destination file. Without this flag, the tool refuses to clobber existing data. Symlink-safe: the destination is unlinked before exclusive create, so an attacker-planted symlink cannot redirect the write.
  -o, --output PATH            Explicit output path. Default: FILE with .prot stripped for file input, stdout for stdin.
  --scope user|machine         Key-derivation scope. 'user' (default) — key bound to current OS user, decryptable only by that user on that machine. 'machine' — key bound to machine credential, decryptable by any user on that machine (Windows needs DPAPI LocalMachine access; macOS needs sudo for System Keychain; Linux: unsupported — tool exits with usage error).
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Examples:
  unprotect secrets.json.prot                                             Decrypt to secrets.json (implicit .prot-suffix strip)
  unprotect secrets.json.prot -o /tmp/out.json                            Decrypt to an explicit output path
  unprotect config.prot --in-place              
[truncated]
